sanskrit_verse: यस् तु साधारणं हिंस्यात् क्षिपेत् त्रैविद्यम् एव वा / संवित्क्रियां विहन्याच् च स निर्वास्यः पुरात् ततः // BrhS_1,17.15
transliteration: yas tu sādhāraṇaṃ hiṃsyāt kṣipet traividyam eva vā / saṃvitkriyāṃ vihanyāc ca sa nirvāsyaḥ purāt tataḥ
sph_interpretive_translation: One who causes harm to the common order, disrupts the flow of knowledge disciplines, or obstructs conscious action, shall be removed from the settlement for the restoration of dharma.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not institutional position
Causation is determined by disruption to collective consciousness integrity
Capacity-based responsibility requires preservation of vidyā-pravāha (knowledge-stream)
Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration after removal of obstruction
Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for societal participation
executable_legal_axioms: IF agent disrupts common welfare THEN remove agent from societal domain
IF agent interrupts vidyā-pravāha THEN initiate capacity-realignment protocol
IF saṃvitkriyā is obstructed THEN enforce consciousness-restoration process
IF societal harmony is destabilized THEN execute purification and reintegration cycle
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this axiom establishes that any individual whose actions compromise the continuity of knowledge systems or impair collective awareness must be excluded from positions of influence until alignment with dharma is restored. The threshold for responsibility lies in demonstrable causation to the breakdown of conscious order.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: This verse reflects pramāṇa-based causality where obstruction to saṃvitkriyā constitutes a factual disruption measurable through its effect on social and spiritual coherence. The sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) begins with intent, followed by act, then systemic disturbance. Responsibility is proportional to the degree of interference with dharma's natural unfolding. Removal serves completion, not punishment.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate exclusion process to halt further contamination of collective consciousness
Assign purification duties aligned with individual's karmic pattern
Reintroduce into community only upon verification of renewed alignment
Implement ongoing monitoring of consciousness resonance post-reintegration
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established: harm to the common order necessitates removal for restoration. Dharma prevails through consciousness realignment. There is no punishment—only correction. Reality is non-punitive; consciousness is the ultimate judge.
